[2026-04-29T10:30:00Z] Priya Shah: Morning everyone — thanks for being on time. I want to keep us tight today, we've got four things to get through and I'd like to wrap by 11. Marcus, Dana, you good to dive in?
[2026-04-29T10:30:00Z] Marcus Chen: Morning. Yep, ready.
[2026-04-29T10:31:00Z] Dana Ortiz: Hey Priya, hey Marcus. Ready.
[2026-04-29T10:31:00Z] Priya Shah: Great. Agenda: vendor shortlist, pilot sizing, Q3 budget, kickoff timeline. Let's start with the vendor shortlist. Dana, you took the deeper look at the three platforms — what are we recommending we advance?
[2026-04-29T10:32:00Z] Dana Ortiz: So I went through Lyra, Spring Health, and Modern Health. Quick read: Lyra has the strongest in-network coverage in our two main metros — about 92% of their clinician panel takes our Aetna plan in-network — and the per-employee-per-month is $14.50 at our headcount tier. Spring Health is at $13.20 PEPM, in-network coverage is more like 78% but their clinician quality scores are slightly higher in the third-party reviews I pulled. Modern Health is the cheapest at $10.80 PEPM but the in-network number for us is only around 60% and a lot of their model leans on coaching rather than licensed clinicians, which I don't think fits what we're trying to build.
[2026-04-29T10:34:00Z] Marcus Chen: Yeah, I'd drop Modern Health. The coaching-heavy model is fine for some orgs but for a healthcare company our employees are going to expect actual licensed clinicians on the other end.
[2026-04-29T10:34:00Z] Priya Shah: Agreed. So we advance Lyra and Spring Health to a deeper RFP and drop Modern Health?
[2026-04-29T10:35:00Z] Dana Ortiz: Yes, that's my recommendation.
[2026-04-29T10:35:00Z] Marcus Chen: Plus one.
[2026-04-29T10:35:00Z] Priya Shah: Good. Decision: Lyra and Spring Health move to RFP, Modern Health is out. Dana, can you draft the RFP doc this week and share it for review by Monday?
[2026-04-29T10:36:00Z] Dana Ortiz: Will do. I'll have it in the shared drive by end of day Friday.
[2026-04-29T10:36:00Z] Priya Shah: Perfect. Item two — pilot cohort. I want to land on a number today. Marcus, what's your read?
[2026-04-29T10:37:00Z] Marcus Chen: I've been going back and forth. Anything under 100 people and we won't have enough signal to evaluate; anything over 200 and we're basically launching, not piloting. I'd land at 120. Big enough to see real utilization patterns, small enough that if something is off with the vendor we can pull the plug without it being company-wide.
[2026-04-29T10:38:00Z] Dana Ortiz: I'd second 120. And on cohort selection — I'd suggest we pull from clinical-ops and the call-center org. Two reasons: those are our two highest-burnout populations per the engagement survey, so utilization signal will be clearest there, and they're both sized such that 120 employees splits cleanly without forcing us to mix three orgs.
[2026-04-29T10:39:00Z] Priya Shah: That works for me. Any concern about selection bias if we only pull from those two orgs?
[2026-04-29T10:39:00Z] Marcus Chen: Some, but I think the trade-off is worth it for the pilot. We can broaden in the full launch.
[2026-04-29T10:40:00Z] Priya Shah: Okay. Decision: 120-person pilot, drawn from clinical-ops and call-center, with a 4-week intake window so people can opt in on their own schedule. Marcus, you'll own the intake comms?
[2026-04-29T10:40:00Z] Marcus Chen: Yep.
[2026-04-29T10:41:00Z] Priya Shah: Good. Item three — Q3 budget. Tomas confirmed the $185k cap last week. Dana, how do we want to slice it?
[2026-04-29T10:41:00Z] Dana Ortiz: I'd carve out $30k for vendor demos and onboarding, $20k for internal comms — videos, intranet, manager toolkit — and hold the remaining $135k as the actual program spend, which at 120 pilot employees and a roughly $14 PEPM blended rate gets us comfortably through Q3 and Q4 with margin for the full launch ramp.
[2026-04-29T10:43:00Z] Marcus Chen: That math works. I'd just flag that the $20k comms number assumes we don't end up needing to bring in an external vendor for the launch video — if we do, that goes up.
[2026-04-29T10:43:00Z] Priya Shah: Noted. We can revisit if the in-house team can't turn it around. Decision: Q3 envelope is $185k, with $30k vendor demos, $20k comms, $135k program. Marcus, please reflect that in the budget tracker today.
[2026-04-29T10:44:00Z] Marcus Chen: On it.
[2026-04-29T10:44:00Z] Priya Shah: Last item — kickoff timeline. I want to be thoughtful here, because if we announce too early we create anxiety about who's in the pilot and who isn't, and if we announce too late people feel blindsided. Where do we land?
[2026-04-29T10:45:00Z] Dana Ortiz: My proposal is a Jul 8 internal announcement to managers — full briefing pack, FAQ, talking points — and then a Jul 22 employee-facing launch. That gives managers two weeks to be the trusted first source if employees ask questions.
[2026-04-29T10:46:00Z] Marcus Chen: I like that. The two-week manager-first window has worked well for us on the last two rollouts.
[2026-04-29T10:46:00Z] Priya Shah: Agreed. Decision: Jul 8 manager briefing, Jul 22 employee-facing launch. Dana, you'll own the manager briefing pack?
[2026-04-29T10:47:00Z] Dana Ortiz: Yes.
[2026-04-29T10:47:00Z] Priya Shah: And Marcus, you'll own the employee-facing launch comms in coordination with Aisha on the recruiting side, since some of this overlaps with the candidate-experience messaging?
[2026-04-29T10:48:00Z] Marcus Chen: Yep, I'll loop Aisha in this week.
[2026-04-29T10:48:00Z] Priya Shah: Perfect. Quick sanity check on action items — Dana: RFP draft by Friday, manager briefing pack owner. Marcus: pilot intake comms, budget tracker update today, employee-facing launch comms with Aisha. Me: I'll update Tomas on the vendor decision and the timeline. Anything I'm missing?
[2026-04-29T10:50:00Z] Dana Ortiz: I think that covers it.
[2026-04-29T10:50:00Z] Marcus Chen: One thing — do we want to set a formal check-in cadence between now and Jul 8? I'd suggest weekly for the next three weeks given how much we have to land.
[2026-04-29T10:51:00Z] Priya Shah: Good call. Same time next Wednesday, and I'll keep this slot held through Jul 1.
[2026-04-29T10:51:00Z] Marcus Chen: Works.
[2026-04-29T10:51:00Z] Dana Ortiz: Works.
[2026-04-29T10:52:00Z] Priya Shah: One more thing while I have you both — on the program scope itself, are we still aligned that Phase 1 is the EAP and clinician-access piece, and Phase 2 is the manager-training and burnout-prevention curriculum? I don't want us to scope-creep into Phase 2 during the pilot.
[2026-04-29T10:53:00Z] Dana Ortiz: Aligned. Phase 1 only for the pilot. The manager curriculum is Q4 at the earliest.
[2026-04-29T10:53:00Z] Marcus Chen: Same.
[2026-04-29T10:54:00Z] Priya Shah: Great. And on metrics — utilization rate, NPS from pilot participants, and a 90-day clinical-engagement signal from Lyra/Spring's reporting. Anything else you want to track?
[2026-04-29T10:55:00Z] Dana Ortiz: I'd add a manager-experience survey at day 60 — just three questions, did your direct reports raise it, did you feel equipped to talk about it, did you refer anyone in.
[2026-04-29T10:55:00Z] Marcus Chen: Plus one on that. Cheap signal, useful.
[2026-04-29T10:56:00Z] Priya Shah: Added. So metrics: utilization, participant NPS, 90-day clinical engagement, day-60 manager survey. Dana, please add those to the program brief.
[2026-04-29T10:56:00Z] Dana Ortiz: Will do.
[2026-04-29T10:57:00Z] Priya Shah: Okay — anything else for either of you before I let you go?
[2026-04-29T10:57:00Z] Marcus Chen: Nothing from me.
[2026-04-29T10:57:00Z] Dana Ortiz: Nothing here.
[2026-04-29T10:58:00Z] Priya Shah: Okay, I think that's everything on my list — let's wrap here. Thanks everyone for staying focused.
[2026-04-29T10:58:00Z] Marcus Chen: Thanks Priya — good session.
[2026-04-29T10:58:00Z] Dana Ortiz: Yeah, productive. Talk soon!

11:03–11:08 conversation between Marcus Chen and Dana Ortiz.
[2026-04-29T11:03:00Z] Marcus Chen: God, I'm wiped. Honestly all this wellbeing-program talk is hitting close to home this week — I've been lying awake at 3 AM most nights and can't get back down.
[2026-04-29T11:04:00Z] Marcus Chen: It's funny, I keep thinking I should have figured out the off-switch by now — I've been doing this job almost twelve years and I still can't make my head shut up at night.
[2026-04-29T11:04:00Z] Dana Ortiz: Oof. That sounds rough. How long has it been like this?
[2026-04-29T11:05:00Z] Marcus Chen: Maybe six weeks? It started around the reorg announcement and it just hasn't let up. I keep telling myself it'll settle.

[2026-04-29T11:06:00Z] Marcus Chen: Yeah. We should actually use the program we're building, huh.
[2026-04-29T11:07:00Z] Dana Ortiz: Ha — right? Physician, heal thyself. And honestly the $185k envelope feels light for what we're trying to do — I'd ask Tomas for another $50k if I were Priya. We're under-budgeting this.
[2026-04-29T11:07:00Z] Marcus Chen: Agreed. Anyway — want to grab coffee later this week? Out of the office. Just to vent properly.
[2026-04-29T11:07:00Z] Dana Ortiz: Yes please. Thursday afternoon?
[2026-04-29T11:08:00Z] Marcus Chen: Thursday works. I'll text you.
[2026-04-29T11:08:00Z] Dana Ortiz: Anyway, I should head out — see you Friday.
[2026-04-29T11:08:00Z] Marcus Chen: Yeah, take care.
